disposition_reason: Onion and carrot trace elements: Table II ranges and means plus text means for As, Cd, Pb and others (dry matter).

study.design: Survey of locally grown onion bulbs and carrot roots for 17 trace and 5 major elements
study.origin: Farmlands and allotment gardens across Latvia
study.market: Obtained at markets or directly from farmers and households
study.method: HNO3/H2O2 wet digestion; flame AAS (Perkin Elmer AAnalyst 200) for Ca, Fe, K, Mg, Na, Cu, Mn, Zn; ICP-MS for other trace elements
study.qa: CRMs CS-CR-2 carrot root powder and NCS ZC73017 apple; Cd by ICP-MS 0.0051 vs certified 0.0058 mg/kg, Pb 0.077 vs 0.084

controls.outcome: Onions from farmland had significantly higher Sr, Ni, Cd, Se and Co; allotment carrots had significantly more Zn, Mn and Rb; subgroup values not printed

unresolved: Ca, K, Mg and Na (Table III) are macro-elements and are not recorded as findings.
Farmland vs allotment subgroup values are not printed for trace elements.
Detection limits are not printed; AAS gave Pb <0.1 mg/kg for the CRM (certified 0.084), so Pb and Cd at 0.05 mg/kg DM rely on ICP-MS.
The Pb and Cd sentence is ambiguous about which value belongs to which element and vegetable.
